<div id="how-to-embed-shiny" class="section level2">
<h2>How to embed <em>Shiny</em></h2>
<p>Static blog systems such as Blogdown or Quarto cannot run a Shiny server inside an R Markdown or Quarto document. The usual solution is to host the Shiny app separately, then embed it in the page with an <code>iframe</code>.</p>
<p>The direct HTML version is written outside the chunk:<br />
<code>&lt;iframe src="https://liuyanguu.shinyapps.io/bcl_app/" width="1000" height="800"&gt;&lt;/iframe&gt;</code></p>
<p>There is also a built-in function in <em>knitr</em> that does the same thing inside a chunk. The main difference is that we can only set <code>height</code>, and the Shiny app may appear slightly differently, with the <strong>sidebarPanel</strong> at the top and the <strong>mainPanel</strong> beneath it.</p>
<pre class="r"><code>knitr::include_app(&quot;https://liuyanguu.shinyapps.io/bcl_app/&quot;, height = &quot;100%&quot;)
# by the way, you can also embed your slides in a similar way, for example:
knitr::include_url(&#39;https://timmastny.rbind.io/slides/first_presentation#2&#39;)</code></pre>
</div>
<div id="my-shiny-app-example" class="section level2">
<h2>My <em>Shiny</em> app example</h2>
<p>I modified the <a href="https://deanattali.com/blog/building-shiny-apps-tutorial/">excellent example and tutorial</a> by Dean Attali, who is also the author of <em>ggExtra</em>’s marginal plot. I found it clearer than the Shiny training materials I had used before.<br />
Thanks a lot. Yes, I donated.</p>
<p>If this embedding does not display well on your screen, here is <a href="https://liuyanguu.shinyapps.io/bcl_app/">the link to the app</a>.
<iframe src="https://liuyanguu.shinyapps.io/bcl_app/" width="1000" height="800"></iframe></p>
<p><strong>The code for the app</strong><br />
All the code is in one file. I did not split the UI and server into separate files.<br />
The code is hosted <a href="https://github.com/liuyanguu/shiny_app/blob/master/bcl_app.R">on GitHub</a>.</p>
</div>
